name: Starter: Albanian
about: Albanian in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Albanian order.

words.jam: be (jam: I am; je: you are; është: is; janë: are)
words.kam: have (ke: you have; ka: has, there is)
words.të: (before a verb: to); the (before some describing words)

te-lutem.about: Literally I beg you, to someone you call ti; ju lutem to someone you call ju.

me-falni.about: Literally forgive me, to someone you call ju; më fal to a friend.

Unë pi çaj dhe ujë dhe.
Unë pi ujë dhe kafe dhe.
Përshëndetje, një dhe kafe, të lutem.

items.text: Një çaj dhe një ujë, të lutem.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Një çaj dhe një ujë, lutem të.
Një dhe çaj një ujë, të lutem.

concept.line: A verb's ending says who does it, so unë (I) and ti (you) are usually left out: jetoj (I live), jeton (you live), jetojmë (we live).
jam (I am), je, është… and kam (I have), ke, ka…; Albanian has hunger and cold where English is hungry and cold: Kam uri (I-have hunger), Kam ftohtë (I-have cold).
my comes after the noun and matches it: shoku im (friend-the my), motra ime (sister-the my), prindërit e mi (parents-the the my).

words.means: kam = I have; ke = you have

concept.line: A often starts a yes-or-no question (A ke fëmijë?

words.means: flet = speak, speaks; flas = I speak
kuptoj = I understand; kupton = you understand

concept.line: nuk goes before the verb and any little pronoun in front of it: Nuk e di (not it I-know).

words.means: jetoj = I live; jeton = live, lives
shkoj = I go; shkon = go, goes

concept.line: Most describing words come after the noun with a little word of their own (i, e, të or së) that matches it: një shtëpi e madhe (a house the big), një qen të zi (a dog the black, as the object).
